info.title: API.SH: Google
info.description: The Google API from API.SH: public Google data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Events from Google's Events box for a query such as "concerts in austin": title, kind of event, date and time, venue, place, day label (Today, Tomorrow, Fri, Oct 30) and the Google entity id with a link to it. `date` narrows to today, tomorrow, week, weekend, next_week or month. Google shows up to about 8-10 events per query (`next_page` is null); `thumbnail` is the event picture (an https URL, or an inline data:image URI when Google embeds it). Use a place in the query, or `location`. Google shows the Events box only with an English interface and not for EU/EEA countries, so `language` other than en is searched as en and an EU/EEA `country` (de, fr, bg, ...) as gb, with `location` (else the country) still choosing the place; the response then has `adjusted` with the requested and used values. When Google shows no events for the search the call answers 200 with `count: 0`, an empty `events` list and a `message`. Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 2 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-events

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: today, tomorrow, week, weekend, next_week, month.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Results country (gl), e.g. us, gb, in. EU/EEA countries are searched as gb (Google has no Events box there); set `location` to the city.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Interface language (hl). The Events box is English-only: other languages are searched as en.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: City/region to search from, e.g. Austin,Texas,United States.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Google Hotels results (google.com/travel): price from, currency, rating, reviews, hotel class and type, amenities, deal, images and `property_token` (= `entity_id`, for /google/v1/hotels/property, /prices and /reviews). Prices are in the requested `currency` (`currency` in the response says which one Google showed; `currency_note` when it differs). Dates, guests, hotel class, amenities, free cancellation, deals, eco-certified, vacation rentals, bedrooms and bathrooms go to Google; `min_price`, `max_price`, `rating` and `sort` apply to the page of results Google returned (about 18-20 properties, one page). The filters used are echoed in `filters`. Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 3 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-hotels

get.description:
A hotel's Google reviews: rating, text, date, author, photos, owner reply, per-topic ratings; with the place's rating and review count. Pass a property's `entity_id` from /google/v1/hotels as `property_token` (or `q`: the hotel name and city). Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; null on the last page. Vacation rentals (`type` "vacation_rental") have no Google reviews: their reviews come from travel sites, and the response lists each site's score, review count and link (`sources`) with its latest review in `reviews` (one page, `next_cursor` null).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-hotels-reviews

get.description:
Google Jobs listings: title, company, location, source, posted, salary, schedule, perks, highlights (qualifications, benefits, responsibilities), the full description and every Apply option (the first one resolved to its real URL), plus `detected_extensions` (posted_at, schedule_type, salary, work_from_home, health_insurance, dental_coverage, paid_time_off, no_degree) and `job_highlights` (title + items). 10 listings per page, up to page 5: pass `next_page` back as `page`; `next_page` is null on the last page (deeper pages take longer, and cost more: page 1 is the route price, page N above 1 adds 7 credits per page, e.g. page 2 = 16 credits). Without a place in `q`, the query is sent as "<q> jobs in <location>" (the first two parts of `location`, else the country; default the United States), because Google Jobs answers searches without a place with no matches; `search_parameters.place` shows the place used. Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 2 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-jobs

parameters.description: Page of 10 jobs (1-5). Pass `next_page` from the previous response; null on the last page.

parameters.name: resolve

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Results country (gl), e.g. us, gb, de.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: City/region to search from, e.g. Austin,Texas,United States.

Google Lens results for an image URL: visual matches (title, link, source, domain, thumbnail, full-size image with its size, price and stock when Google shows them), products (the matches with a price), web results, related searches and the AI overview of the image. `type=exact_matches` (or `exact=1` with the other types) adds exact matches: pages that use the same image, with date and image size. The image must be publicly reachable; an image Google cannot read answers 400. One page of results (`next_page` is null). Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 2 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-lens

get.description:
Google results with every Google option: country / location / language, time and date range, result type (web, news, images, videos, shopping, books, forums), site and file-type filters, SafeSearch, desktop or mobile, and up to 100 results per call (`limit`). All options are free except `limit`, which loads one results page per 10 results. Pass `next_page` from the previous response; `next_page` is null on the last page. Each web result has `url` (the exact address) and `google_link`. Google now holds some result links on a verification page for about a minute after a search, so `url` can be null: then `site_url` gives the site and `url_guess` the address rebuilt from the green breadcrumb (null when Google shortened it). `discussions_and_forums` lists the forum and discussion threads among the results (Reddit, Quora and other forums) with their community, comment or answer count, age and top answer; `type=forums` searches Google's Forums tab. Every result also has `domain` and `displayed_url` (the green breadcrumb, or the site line of a video or forum card). Pass `fast=true` for answers in about 3 s instead of about 8 s: links are not resolved, `url` is Google's redirect link (it opens the page when visited) and `links_resolved` is false.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 3 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search query (also accepted as query or keyword).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Results for this country (Google gl, and the location defaults to it). Two-letter code.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Search as if from this place, e.g. `Austin,Texas,United States` (Google uule). Default: the country.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Interface language (Google hl), e.g. en, de, pt-BR.

parameters.name: lr
parameters.description: Only results in these languages, e.g. `en` or `en|de`.

parameters.name: cr
parameters.description: Only results from these countries, e.g. `US` or `US|GB`.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: Only results from the past hour, day, week, month or year; `day_3` = past 3 days.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: Only results up to this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: tbs
parameters.description: Raw Google tbs filter, combined with the options above.

parameters.name: autocorrect
parameters.description: 0 searches the query exactly as typed (no spelling correction).

parameters.name: filetype
parameters.description: Only this file type, e.g. pdf.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: web (default), news, images, videos, shopping, books or forums (Google's Forums tab: discussion threads, laid out like web results).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (10 results each). Pass next_page from the previous response.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many results (1-100). Each 10 results is one more results page.

parameters.name: resolve
parameters.description: 1 (default) turns Google's /goto links into the real URLs; 0 skips that.

parameters.name: fast
parameters.description: Faster answers (about 3 s instead of about 8 s): result links are not resolved, so `url` is Google's redirect link, which opens the page when visited (or the direct address when Google links straight to it). `displayed_url` (the line Google shows under the title) is always filled, `domain` whenever the result shows its address or a well-known site name, and the response has `links_resolved: false`. Same price. Default false.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: color, grayscale, transparent, or a colour: red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink, white, gray, black, brown.

parameters.name: image_format
parameters.description: jpg, png, gif, bmp, svg, webp, ico, raw.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: short (<4 min), medium (4-20 min), long (>20 min).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
